correctness.rationale: The baseline n+1 follows from chain-graph Theorem 5 and a legal (n+1)-sequence; general atomic edge theorem yields n+2 upper bound. Explicit four-case vertex sequences cover all nonpendant deletions and were reconstructed against closed-neighborhood footprints, including reflected edges and n=3 boundaries. For pendant deletion the remaining component has the exact chain-graph twin-class pattern yielding n; adding the isolate gives n+1. Exact independent bitmask DP tests all 119 individual deleted-edge cases at n=2..8 and verifies 4,900 explicit witnesses at n=3..30. Finite checks are corroboration only; the written constructions and known theorems cover every n>=3.

value.rationale: The theorem completely solves a canonical infinite parameter family of exact atomic-change equality cases: every nonpendant edge realizes sharp +1 sensitivity, while precisely two pendant edges do not. It is a meaningful structural sharpness classification for an established graph invariant, requires uniform constructive sequence families and graph-specific boundary analysis, and is not an arbitrary numerical slice or a restatement of the general inequality.
